score_notes.A: Front matter fine (two-level categories, use_math with $$ at L439/L696, no H1). Deductions: the TL;DR (L13-15) is two dense paragraphs; the same install command appears twice (L73, L331).
score_notes.B: Natural Korean, consistent 입니다 register, no colon-after-다 lists. Deductions: six '곧/즉' restatements (e.g. L62 '별도의 Ray 액터, 곧 별도 프로세스'), and L48 '정리하면 Ray Serve는 ... 서빙 라이브러리입니다' repeats L19.
score_notes.C: L241 '아래 팬아웃 예제처럼' points to an example that does not exist (the next code block is the streaming one). L241 also cites a '_hello_handle' ingress example, and L237 an Adder/Combiner graph, neither of which is shown. There are two conflicting text_ml.py versions: L178 says the file uses load_t5/generate helpers, while L336 says the file does not use them. L493 runs 'serve_quickstart:translator_app', but the post never names that file. L128 says the HTTP proxy runs on the head node by default, yet the L642 table gives the proxy_location default as EveryNode, and the two are never reconciled.
score_notes.D: Good help where things get hard: the power-of-two worked table (L160-168), the draining arithmetic (L792), and the query-param pitfall (L445). L42 is a little promotional padding.
score_notes.E: Tables and ASCII flow diagrams sit where they are discussed. The official architecture figure is missing. The 100KiB table (L230-233) repeats the L172 prose.
score_notes.F: All 15 sampled claims are supported. One invented-attribution case (-2): L178 says 'text_ml.py에서 ... t5-small 로딩과 생성 단계는 load_t5, generate 함수가 맡습니다', but the official text_ml.py has no such helpers (the generator's own warning flagged this too). That snippet also drops Summarizer's min_length=5.
score_notes.T1: The running example runs as pasted. On Ray 2.60.0 with a private cluster, text_ml:app returned 200 with French text, the reconfigure version switches to German, and the FastAPI query-param client, both streaming examples and the hello example also work. Gaps: the serve_quickstart.py file name is never given (L493), and the deploy YAML (L614-636) has no working_dir, so 'serve deploy' to a cluster started elsewhere relies on text_ml being importable there.
score_notes.T2: Covers the important topics in a sensible order. The Ray Data LLM batch section (L872-930) sits at the edge of the source scope.
score_notes.T3: Strong coverage of internals: actors and the request path, power-of-two routing, the object store, layered fault tolerance, autoscaler vs Ray Autoscaler, per-caller backpressure, proxy health and draining with a load balancer, observability, and when to choose it. Design advice reads as advice (L723, L958). The sources include a duplicate older-docs page (releases-2.59.0, L988), but nothing in the post relies on it alone.
